linkedin.activityText: Alexis Ohanian Sr. Alexis Ohanian Sr. 8h Alexis Ohanian Sr. shared this I was very excited to lead this at pre-seed because I want my kids to have a healthy relationship with tech while ALSO spending as much time in the world as possible - and this is the first phone that actually had the goal of keeping kids engaged in the WORLD. Lemme know what you think - we just launched and we're already at thousands of pre-orders Sam Terris Sam Terris 17h Alexis Ohanian Sr. shared this Freckle is the first kids phone built for real-world adventure. It is available for pre-order today, and we will begin shipping in December of this year. I’m still a rookie when it comes to fatherhood. It can feel like an impossible sum of new information to get my arms around and the protocols have become rather data-centric & exacting. I sometimes feel the mild judgement of older generations who are skeptical of our obsession around naps, feeding schedules, etc. But I think for the most part, we’ve made a lot of progress in our understanding of creating systems to help kids best self-actualize. One area where we seem to have moved in the wrong direction, however, is kids’ independence. They are spending remarkably little time exploring, playing, and just being kids outside the supervision of an adult. It’s so hard for a kid to develop in an environment where a parent is hovering over their shoulder. There’s no space to experiment, to expand. At the same time, passive screen consumption has gone way up. A loss of physical freedom was replaced with essentially unfettered digital access. In response, the market has produced a bunch of products oriented around parent anxiety, completely optimized for the job of giving parents more control. Billed as tools for safety, they're generally used as ankle monitors and can make it even harder for kids to develop autonomy. At Freckle, we believe the best product in this space will focus less on restriction, and more on safely empowering kids. We started by asking kids what they want, designed to their sensibilities, and ultimately developed tools to give them more agency, and more space to explore the world beyond the screen. We created a product where parents can meaningfully participate beyond surveillance & control. Right-sizing technology doesn't have to mean stripping it to its studs. Freckle is fun! And it is exactly what I want for my own family. We haven’t played a match yet and already have two Day 1s campaigning to lead The Wall aka Fan section 🔥

Think you can bring the noise? Tag your loudest friends🧡 💪🏐🪐

Still not over this weekend’s brand launch and fan fest! 🧡💫

Shoutout to everyone who came to @intuitdome to celebrate @laorbitvb!

I feel so lucky to get to play volleyball in my hometown and be part of building something so special in LA. Can’t wait for season 🚀

We felt alllllllll the LOVB over the weekend! 🥲🧡

#LAOrbit #EverythingRevolvesAroundHer

Met @burfordbeachhomes, her daughter @kennedyb.2032, and her incredible mom at our first-ever Fan Fest at @watchme_sportsbar in Long Beach during the @lovb championship weekend in April, the week before I even started this job.

This weekend, I got to be there as Brittny, her mom and her daughter picked out their season tickets for LA Orbit. Three generations, together 🧡🏐🧡

And then I heard what her mom had done the very same day we first met: she got a @laorbitvb (LOVB LA back then!) inspired tattoo. @alexisohanian we may have our first fan ready for that @laorbitvb logo tat 😝 

In all seriousness, this is what being a Day One looks like.

Brittny, I’m never going to forget this! Thank you for believing in us before there was even an LA Orbit to believe in 🥹🧡🏐

@laorbitvb Outside Hitter @madi_kingdon said the goal out loud ➡️ Become the BIGGEST volleyball team in LA! 💫🪐🧡🏐

And based on what we’ve seen so far? I have 0 doubts!
